newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firm on chill, arb from US Gulf closes.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firm on chill, arb from US Gulf closes.

text.p: Firm heating oil demand lifted NWE gas oil cargo and barge premiums on Monday but volume was restricted by the Epiphany holiday in parts of Europe, traders said.
A surge in New York heating oil futures late in the European day closed an arbitrage play from the U.S. Gulf to NWE, further curbing potential European gas oil volume, traders added.
"There's lots of buyers but not so many offers," a cargo trader said of 0.2 percent sulphur European heating oil.
Benchmark IPE Jan and Feb futures rose $4.50 cents to $232 a tonne and $5.75 to $228.75 a tonne respectively.

They were lifted by a sharp rally in NYMEX heating oil built on forecasts of colder U.S. weather. Low sulphur diesel trade was weak and inactive, with premiums sinking to around Feb IPE +$11.50/12.50.
Heating oil refinery grade cargoes were bid around 50 cents firmer at Feb IPE +$8.50 cif Bremen and notionally offered at around Feb IPE +$10.

In barges, refinery grade heating oil traded around $2 firmer at Jan IPE +$3 and $3.25 fob Rotterdam while the market into Amsterdam and Antwerp was offered at Jan IPE +$2. Iced-up canals continued to curb inland barge trade.
